title: Every bounded charge sector has a unique smooth local Lorenz-gauge evolution

bounded_charge_flow.spectral_cutoff: P_N=1_{[-N,N]}(Q) is the self-adjoint charge spectral projector; P_N commutes with Q, exp(i alpha Q), spatial derivatives and the real radial multiplier
bounded_charge_flow.invariant_sector: Initial matter data in ran(P_N) remain in ran(P_N), because D_A, Q^2 and f(||phi||^2) act diagonally in charge and the Maxwell current is scalar-valued
bounded_charge_flow.bounded_generator: Q_N=Q restricted to ran(P_N) is bounded with ||Q_N||<=N, while the internal multiplicity may remain infinite
bounded_charge_flow.lorenz_system: In Lorenz gauge the Maxwell--matter equations form a semilinear Hilbert-valued wave system with at most first spacetime derivatives and smooth polynomial nonlinearities on H^(R+1)xH^R for integer R>=3
bounded_charge_flow.local_theorem: Standard wave Duhamel contraction gives one unique solution (A_N,phi_N) in C([-T_N,T_N];H^(R+1)) intersect C^1([-T_N,T_N];H^R), with phi_N valued in ran(P_N)
bounded_charge_flow.constraint_data: If the initial Lorenz and Gauss compatibility conditions hold, K1374's continuity identity propagates them throughout the local solution
bounded_charge_flow.smooth_persistence: Smooth spatial data with values in a bounded charge sector give a smooth common-core solution on the same local interval
bounded_charge_flow.boundary: The cutoff theorem alone has a cutoff-dependent contraction constant and does not produce a completed unbounded-Q flow, global evolution, source action or physical quotient
